title: New Book on Michael Jackson Explores Singer’s ‘Genius’
main_content:
Michael Jackson’s career began in the mid-1960s before his 10th birthday. As the youngest member of the Jackson 5 and later as a solo artist, Jackson became a global icon. His albums have been sold in more than 400 million copies, earning 13 Grammy awards and spinning dance moves that captivated the world.

Authors, too, have been captivated by the man. Since his death in 2009 at the age of 50, there has been a seemingly endless stream of books written about him. “MJ: The Genius of Michael Jackson” is one of the latest, but not likely the last.

Author Steve Knopper spent three years interviewing more than 400 people who knew Michael Jackson — from relatives and friends to key record executives and celebrities. His goal was to explore what he calls the genius of the King of Pop.

“He was a genius on many levels,” Knopper said. “The three key ones to me were his intuitive singing style, the way he put in those rhythms. Secondly, the way he innovated dance at the time where there wasn’t a lot of dance in the pop culture. Then, thirdly, his songwriting. And I think he doesn’t get enough credit for being a great songwriter.”

One of Jackson’s trademarks was his moonwalk dance, the famous glide that looks like he’s moving forward and backward at the same time.

Knopper says Jackson learned that move from a number of different sources, including himself. But specifically, it came from a group of dancers — Casper Candidate, Cooley Jackson and Jeffrey Daniels — who performed on the popular TV music show, “Soul Train.”

“They had actually done the dance to one of Michael’s songs, ‘Working Day and Night’,” Knopper recalled. “He eventually invited a couple of these guys to teach it to him. I did an interview with Cooley Jackson who explains that Michael kept saying, ‘I’m not getting it.  I’m not getting it.’ It’s a very difficult move to get and it didn’t click till you worked on it and worked on it, and finally Michael got it.”

Jackson’s genius in so many areas is what made him a global cultural phenomenon, whose impact on pop music will be felt for generations to come, Knopper said.

questions.question: Why was the world captivated by Michael Jackson?
options: His ability to sing and dance in perfect harmony.
The unique blend of his intuitive singing, innovative dance, and songwriting.
His extensive influence on rock music and the genre's evolution.
The elaborate concerts and stage performances he organized.
questions.answer: The unique blend of his intuitive singing, innovative dance, and songwriting.

questions.question: What happened after Jackson’s death?
options: A renewed interest in pop music led to a resurgence of similar artists.
Numerous books have been published exploring his life and career.
His music was pulled from circulation due to controversies.
Tributes and memorials were held only in the United States.
questions.answer: Numerous books have been published exploring his life and career.

questions.question: How did Steve Knopper try to find out more about Michael Jackson?
options: By studying Jackson's music and analyzing his albums.
Through interviews with over 400 individuals connected to Jackson.
By attending his concerts and gathering audience feedback.
By reviewing critical articles written about his career.
questions.answer: Through interviews with over 400 individuals connected to Jackson.
